🚨🇲🇽 CNTE'S WORLD CUP THREAT FIZZLES — ISSSTE REPEAL WOULD COST 20% OF GDP, SHEINBAUM SAYS

CNTE's slogan going into the Mundial: "If there's no solution, the ball won't roll." What actually happened: the 12-day Zócalo encampment closed, the march to the Azteca ended peacefully, and teachers chanted "no son maestros" at black-bloc vandals smashing barriers. Sheinbaum on the demand to repeal the 2007 ISSSTE pension law: "very complex to repeal" — cost roughly 20% of GDP. The ball rolled. Mexico beat South Africa 2–0.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 VERACRUZ DRAWS 593,000 TO FREE SALSA FEST — CUBA'S LUCRECIA LEADS CELIA CRUZ TRIBUTE

Salsa Fest 2026 runs June 12–14 at the Salsódromo in Boca del Río — last year's edition drew 593,000 across three days, all free. Gilberto Santa Rosa, Víctor Manuelle, Grupo Niche, Rey Ruiz, La India, Olga Tañón on the bill. Cuban singer Lucrecia leads the Celia Cruz tribute. While Washington sanctions CUPET to starve Havana's grid, Veracruz hosts a Cuban legend before half a million people, for free.

🇲🇽📚 SHEINBAUM ADDS 20,000 FREE ONLINE COLLEGE SEATS — TOWARD 330K NEW HIGHER-ED SLOTS BY 2030

SEP head Mario Delgado opens registration July 20 for 20,000 new spots at the Universidad Abierta y a Distancia de México — 100% online, 100% free. UnADM is already Mexico's 5th-largest public university by enrollment, with 129,000+ students in Mexico and abroad. Sheinbaum's stated target: 330,000 new higher-ed places by 2030. The neoliberal era shut campuses. The 4T builds new ones, free.

🚨🇱🇧 ISRAEL BOMBS BEIRUT ON EVE OF US-IRAN DEAL — TRUMP TELLS BOTH "DON'T BLOW IT"

Israel hit Dahiyeh in southern Beirut on the eve of the US-Iran memorandum signing — 3 dead, 16 wounded per Lebanese authorities. Tehran now calls a deal "impossible," saying Washington "does not have the will or capacity to fulfill its commitments." Trump tells both sides "don't blow this up." The 60-day technical framework was set for Sunday. Israel chose Sunday to bomb it.

REALCLEARWORLD: Trump's Counterproductive Mexico Policy
June 12, 2026 | 🟢

📰 RealClearWorld, of all places. Defense Priorities fellow Daniel DePetris argues Trump's military-threat-and-indict approach is breaking US-Mexico cooperation. His prescription: drop the regime-change theater, support Mexico's own investigations.

DePetris also concedes Sheinbaum cannot ship Morena allies — like Sinaloa governor Rocha Moya — to US courts without splitting her own party, and that military options "typically fragment cartels into more violent factions."

• military force is "wholly ineffective at stopping the drug trade"
• Trump himself called Sheinbaum a "wonderful woman" "doing a stellar job running her country"

NYT: World Cup Ticket Prices in Mexico City Too Expensive for Most Fans
June 12, 2026 | 🟢

📰 Rare straight take from the NYT: opening-match seats ran $3,000–$10,000 in FIFA's second drop. The headline pins the gouge on FIFA's dynamic pricing, not on Sheinbaum or the host country.

Sheinbaum herself said as much when asked why she did not attend the opener: "Tickets are very expensive." Parallel CNN and NPR coverage of the same FIFA pricing scheme reaches the same conclusion.

(Article paywalled — framing assessed from headline + corroborating CNN/NPR reporting.)

USA TODAY: Mexico's president closed schools, ordered remote work because of the World Cup
June 11, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Sheinbaum closes Mexico City schools and orders federal-worker remote work for the World Cup opener — narrowly to ease traffic, with health, security and infrastructure exempted.

The story tacks on the teachers' strike but waves it off as "causes unrelated to the matches" — never naming what the CNTE is actually demanding (reversal of the 2007 ISSSTE pension cut, salary increase, restoration of defined-benefit retirement).

• "This decree is so that the opening ceremony can take place without traffic or problems on World Cup day" — Sheinbaum
• protests over "causes unrelated to the matches"

AP/WAPO: Mexican authorities investigate homicide of mayor in Oaxaca state
June 13, 2026 | 🟡

📰 An Oaxaca mayor asks the state for protection. Weeks later he is shot dead. The AP wire frames it as a threat to "Mexico's efforts to project safety as it co-hosts the World Cup" — not as the predictable result of decades of US-fueled drug war and weapons trafficking that hollowed out municipal governance.

PAN said Joel Bravo had reported he "feared for his life and requested protection" from the state before he was killed in San Miguel Amatitlán.

• "There will not be impunity" — Mexican Security Cabinet
• killing "undermines Mexico's efforts to project safety as it co-hosts the World Cup"

🚨🇲🇽 TRUMP TARIFFS DESTROYED 213,000 INDUSTRIAL JOBS — MORE LOST IN HIS OWN COUNTRY THAN HE'LL EVER ADMIT

Between February 2025 and February 2026, Trump's tariff regime wiped out 213,347 manufacturing jobs across North America — 102,000 in the United States and 111,347 in Mexico.

The wreckage by sector: transport equipment lost 17,200 jobs in the US and 47,436 in Mexico; plastics and rubber lost 14,000 (US) and 11,062 (MX); apparel lost 8,341 in Mexico; machinery lost 10,300 in the US.

The "America First" line collapses on its own data. Tariffs hit US workers harder than they hit Beijing, and integrated supply chains don't care about MAGA rhetoric.

Source: El Economista

🇲🇽🌎 TRUMP KEEPS HITTING TMEC FOR DOMESTIC THEATER — MEXICAN BUSINESS LEADERS SAY THE TREATY ISN'T MOVING

CCE leader José Medina Mora Icaza put it bluntly: "Hay que estar preparados, el presidente Trump seguirá golpeando al T-MEC, seguirá golpeando a México. Para nosotros en el sector empresarial lo importante es que el tratado sigue."

The leverage runs the other way and Trump knows it: Mexico is the primary trading partner for 24 US economic sectors and 26 US states. Even without a formal renewal, the agreement holds for 10 years automatically — 16 years if reconfirmed.

The punches are theater. The integration is structural.

Source: Regeneración
